notes: Company: mid-market SaaS (product analytics) building an in-app assistant + search+summaries for product data
Initial engagement: started on Hosted API (fast prototype). After prototype success, evaluating Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation
Security: InfoSec requires SSO/SAML, SOC2, customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and US-only data residency — critical for procurement
Business goals: tightly control p95 latency for short chat replies, reduce per-token unit cost vs hosted for production traffic, and guarantee isolation for customer data
Quote from product lead: "We need consistent 100–200ms p95 for quick guidance snippets — spikes kill UX."
Procurement: asking for committed capacity pricing (6–12 month) and a blended monthly cap to mitigate burst risk
SE notes: good fit for Redwood Dedicated; recommends 2-node baseline with autoscale burst; suggested quantized open models + smaller low-latency fallback
Security review in progress — shared Redwood security FAQ and SOC2 doc (drive links above). Firewall whitelisting window requested by infra team.
poc_scope: 6-week Dedicated POC: deploy a 2-node dedicated pool in VPC (US), run traffic split vs Hosted API, validate: latency SLOs (p95 <200ms for short chat), embeddings throughput (50 qps), cost per 1k tokens target, and operational playbooks (autoscale, canary, rollback)
canary_plan: Phase 0: baseline measurements on Hosted API for 1 week (latency, token mix, error rates)
Phase 1: deploy Dedicated pool behind feature flag; route 5% production-like traffic for 24–48h
Phase 2: if stable, increase to 25% for 48–72h while exercising edge cases (long context, high token replies)
Phase 3: 100% production routing to Dedicated only after two green windows and cost acceptance
Rollback triggers: sustained error-rate increase >5% vs baseline, p95 latency regression >30%, or tokenization/formatting regressions detected by eval set
Monitoring: use Redwood Console dashboards + custom traces; SE/RD on-call during rollouts
fallback_strategy: Model-variant routing: primary -> quantized larger model (high quality), fallback -> smaller low-latency variant for tail requests
Regional failover: primary region us-east-1, secondary us-west-2; DNS + routing policies with cold-start warmup plan
Hosted API fallback: during capacity exhaust or severe incidents, route non-PII / low-priority traffic to Redwood Hosted API with tag-based tracing
Rollback: automatic canary rollback in console; manual rollback via AE/SE with documented runbook; preserve KV caches where possible to avoid quality cliffs
